title: AES masking PRNG forwards force_masks_i to the lockup override when mask forcing is disabled
claim: When SecAllowForcingMasks is 0, the AES masking PRNG should not let force_masks_i assert the Bivium primitive lockup override. The RTL assigns the override directly from force_masks_i, so an external force request reaches a security-sensitive primitive control even though the compile-time feature gate disables mask forcing.

source_locations.excerpt: SecAllowForcingMasks controls whether force_masks_i may force constant masks.
force_masks_i is marked unused when SecAllowForcingMasks is 0, but bivium_allow_lockup is assigned directly from force_masks_i.
bivium_allow_lockup drives allow_lockup_i on the masking PRNG primitive.
FORCE_MASKS is only applicable if both Masking and SecAllowForcingMasks are set.

security_invariant: With SecAllowForcingMasks disabled, a FORCE_MASKS request must not assert the masking PRNG lockup-override path.

attacker_model.capability: Can exercise the AES auxiliary force-masks control during a side-channel evaluation or fault-oriented test configuration.
preconditions: AES masking PRNG is compiled with SecAllowForcingMasks=0.
The force_masks_i control is driven high while the PRNG is instantiated.

proof_style: Directed single-DUT Verilator witness at the aes_prng_masking boundary.
controls: With force_masks_i=0 and SecAllowForcingMasks=0, the wrapper and primitive lockup-override input both remain 0.
witness: With force_masks_i=1 and SecAllowForcingMasks=0, the wrapper's bivium_allow_lockup and the primitive allow_lockup_i are both observed as 1 even though the secure expectation is 0.
expected_evidence: proof/logs/compile.log records a single-DUT Verilator build of aes_prng_masking with the directed testbench.
proof/logs/run.log records BUG006_CONTROL, BUG006_WITNESS_GATE, and BUG006_WITNESS_PASS.
